question_text: A principal of ₹12,000 is invested at 10% per annum simple interest for 3 years. What is the total amount?
correct_answer: Simple Interest (SI) = Principal × Rate × Time / 100. SI = 12000 × 10 × 3 / 100 = ₹3,600. Total Amount = Principal + SI = 12000 + 3600 = ₹15,600. The key formula is: SI = PRT/100 and Amount = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100). For quick mental calculation: 10% of 12000 = 1200 per year, so 3 years = ₹3600 interest.
key_points: SI = PRT/100
Amount = P + SI
10% annual = 1/10 of principal per year
Always distinguish SI from CI in the problem statement
tip: Bank exams always test whether you use SI or CI formula — read the question carefully for 'simple' or 'compound'.

question_text: What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum compounded annually?
key_points: A = P(1 + R/100)^n for annual compounding
CI = Amount - Principal
Year-by-year method equally valid for 2 years
CI > SI for same principal, rate, time
tip: Effective CI rate for 2 years at R% = 2R + R²/100 — useful shortcut formula.

question_text: A train 120 metres long passes a pole in 10 seconds. At what speed is the train moving? How long to cross a platform 150 metres long?
correct_answer: Speed = Distance/Time = 120/10 = 12 m/s. Convert to km/h: 12 × 18/5 = 43.2 km/h. To cross a platform 150m long: train must cover its own length + platform length = 120 + 150 = 270m. Time = Distance/Speed = 270/12 = 22.5 seconds. Key: when crossing a stationary object, distance = train length. When crossing a platform, distance = train length + platform length.
key_points: Speed = Length of train / Time to pass a pole
Distance to cross platform = Train length + Platform length
m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5
km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18
tip: Two trains moving: if same direction use relative speed (difference), opposite direction use sum of speeds.

question_text: A can do a job in 12 days, B can do it in 15 days. How long will they take together? If A works alone for 4 days, then B joins — how many more days to finish?
correct_answer: A's rate = 1/12 per day. B's rate = 1/15 per day. Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 = 5/60 + 4/60 = 9/60 = 3/20 per day. Together time = 20/3 = 6⅔ days. Second part: A does 4 × (1/12) = 1/3 of job in 4 days. Remaining = 1 - 1/3 = 2/3. Together they do 3/20 per day. Time to finish remaining = (2/3)/(3/20) = (2/3) × (20/3) = 40/9 ≈ 4.44 more days.
key_points: Rate = 1/days, combined rate = sum of individual rates
Fraction of work = Rate × Time
Remaining work / Combined rate = remaining time
LCM method: assign total work as LCM of days
tip: LCM method is faster for exams: take LCM of 12 and 15 = 60 units. A does 5/day, B does 4/day. Together: 9/day. Time = 60/9 = 6⅔ days.

question_text: If the cost price of an article is ₹500 and it is sold at a profit of 20%, what is the selling price? If sold at a 10% loss, what is the selling price?
correct_answer: Profit case: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 = 500 × 120/100 = ₹600. Loss case: SP = CP × (100 - Loss%)/100 = 500 × 90/100 = ₹450. Profit = SP - CP = 600 - 500 = ₹100. Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (100/500) × 100 = 20%. If SP > CP: profit. If SP < CP: loss. Always calculate profit% and loss% on Cost Price, not Selling Price.
key_points: Profit% and Loss% always on CP
CP = SP × 100/(100 + profit%) when SP and profit% given
Marked Price vs Selling Price — discount on Marked Price
tip: If two items sold at same SP with same profit% and loss% — there is ALWAYS a net loss of (common %)²/100.

question_text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 15 minutes. If all three are opened together, how long to fill the tank?
correct_answer: Rate of A = 1/20, B = 1/30 (filling, positive). Rate of C = -1/15 (emptying, negative). Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15. LCM of 20, 30, 15 = 60. Net rate = 3/60 + 2/60 - 4/60 = 1/60 per minute. Time to fill = 60 minutes. If C is an emptying pipe: always subtract its rate. If net rate is negative, tank empties faster than it fills — it can never be filled.
key_points: Filling pipes: positive rate, Emptying pipes: negative rate
Net rate = sum of all individual rates
Take LCM to add fractions easily
If net rate negative: tank can't be filled
tip: Common exam trap: forgetting to subtract the emptying pipe's rate — always read which pipes fill and which empty.

question_text: What is the simple interest rate if ₹5,000 becomes ₹6,500 in 5 years?
correct_answer: SI = Amount - Principal = 6500 - 5000 = ₹1,500. Formula: SI = PRT/100. 1500 = 5000 × R × 5/100. 1500 = 250R. R = 1500/250 = 6% per annum. Verification: SI = 5000 × 6 × 5/100 = 1500. Amount = 5000 + 1500 = 6500. ✓ When finding rate: R = (SI × 100)/(P × T).
key_points: SI = Amount - Principal first
Always verify your answer by substituting back
Rate per annum unless otherwise stated
tip: If question gives monthly rate, convert to annual by multiplying by 12 before applying SI formula.

question_text: In a mixture of 40 litres, milk and water are in the ratio 3:2. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3:4?
correct_answer: Initial ratio 3:2, total = 40 litres. Milk = 3/5 × 40 = 24 litres. Water = 2/5 × 40 = 16 litres. Milk doesn't change, so new ratio 3:4 means: milk stays 24 litres, new water = ? 24/new_water = 3/4. New water = 32 litres. Additional water = 32 - 16 = 16 litres must be added. Check: 24:32 = 3:4. ✓
key_points: Find actual quantities from initial ratio and total
Identify which component is constant
Set up equation with the final required ratio
The constant component bridges old and new ratios
tip: If milk is removed instead of water added — the component remaining constant changes. Identify it carefully.

question_text: A shopkeeper marks a product 40% above cost price and then gives a 25% discount. What is the profit or loss percentage?
correct_answer: Let CP = ₹100. Marked Price = 100 + 40% of 100 = ₹140. Selling Price = 140 - 25% of 140 = 140 - 35 = ₹105. Profit = SP - CP = 105 - 100 = ₹5. Profit% = 5/100 × 100 = 5%. Formula shortcut: Net effect = (m - d - m×d/100)% where m = markup%, d = discount%. = 40 - 25 - (40×25)/100 = 15 - 10 = 5% profit.
key_points: Markup is always on Cost Price
Discount is always on Marked Price
Net effect formula: m - d - md/100
Profit if SP > CP, Loss if SP < CP
tip: If discount = markup × (100/(100+markup)), it results in exactly no profit no loss — useful reverse calculation.

question_text: The average of 5 numbers is 25. If one number is removed, the average becomes 22. What is the removed number?
correct_answer: Sum of 5 numbers = 5 × 25 = 125. Sum of remaining 4 numbers = 4 × 22 = 88. Removed number = 125 - 88 = 37. Key principle: Total sum = Average × Count. Always find total sums before and after, then take the difference. This approach works for all average-based problems: adding numbers, removing numbers, or changing values.
key_points: Sum = Average × Count
Removed number = old sum - new sum
Works for adding: added number = new sum - old sum
Average change × remaining count = amount changed
tip: Quick method: if average drops by 3 (25→22) with 4 remaining, deficit covered by removed number = 37 - 25 = 12 + 25 = 37.

question_text: A 20% increase in the price of an item and a 20% decrease — is the net effect neutral?
correct_answer: No, the net effect is always a LOSS of (20)²/100 = 4%. Proof: Start with ₹100. After 20% increase: ₹120. After 20% decrease on ₹120: 120 × 80/100 = ₹96. Net loss = ₹4 on ₹100 = 4% loss. General formula: net effect = -x²/100 where x is the equal percentage increase and decrease. This is always a loss — percentage increases and decreases of equal magnitude don't cancel out.
key_points: Equal % increase then decrease = net loss of x²/100
Order doesn't matter: decrease first, then increase = same result
Mathematical proof: (1+x)(1-x) = 1-x²
Same principle in profit/loss when buying and selling
tip: This is a classic bank exam trick question — interviewers test whether candidates know it's not neutral.

question_text: What is the probability of drawing 2 red balls from a bag containing 4 red and 6 blue balls?
correct_answer: Total balls = 10. Ways to draw 2 from 10 = C(10,2) = 10!/(2!×8!) = 45. Ways to draw 2 red from 4 red = C(4,2) = 4!/(2!×2!) = 6. Probability = Favorable outcomes / Total outcomes = 6/45 = 2/15. For probability without replacement: alternatively P = (4/10) × (3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15. Same answer. Combinations method is cleaner when drawing multiple items simultaneously.
key_points: P = Favorable / Total outcomes
Without replacement: multiply conditional probabilities
Simultaneous draw = without replacement
tip: With replacement vs without replacement — draw with replacement means same probability each time; without replacement changes denominator.

question_text: If X is 25% less than Y and Y is 25% more than Z, what percentage is X of Z?
correct_answer: Let Z = 100. Y = Z + 25% of Z = 125. X = Y - 25% of Y = 125 - 31.25 = 93.75. X/Z × 100 = 93.75%. So X is 93.75% of Z. Important: 25% less than Y means 75% of Y (not 75% of Z). Common mistake: applying percentages to different bases. Always clarify the base of the percentage in each step.
key_points: 25% less than Y means 0.75 × Y
25% more than Z means 1.25 × Z
Start with a convenient base value (100)
Check which value each percentage is applied to
tip: Percentage problems: always identify the base explicitly — '25% of what' determines the calculation.

question_text: A boat travels 30 km upstream in 5 hours and 30 km downstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water and the stream speed.
correct_answer: Upstream speed = 30/5 = 6 km/h. Downstream speed = 30/3 = 10 km/h. Boat speed in still water = (Downstream + Upstream)/2 = (10+6)/2 = 8 km/h. Stream speed = (Downstream - Upstream)/2 = (10-6)/2 = 2 km/h. Key: upstream = boat speed - stream speed, downstream = boat speed + stream speed. These two equations give us the boat and stream speeds separately.
key_points: Upstream = Boat speed - Stream speed
Downstream = Boat speed + Stream speed
Still water speed = (D + U)/2
Stream speed = (D - U)/2
tip: If asked for time to travel a distance in still water, use still water speed directly — stream has zero effect.

question_text: In how many ways can 5 books be arranged on a shelf? In how many ways can 3 books be selected from 5 for a prize?
correct_answer: Arrangement (Permutation) of all 5 books = 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 ways. Selection (Combination) of 3 from 5 = C(5,3) = 5!/(3! × 2!) = 120/(6×2) = 10 ways. Key distinction: Permutation is for arrangements where order matters (P = n!/(n-r)!). Combination is for selections where order does not matter (C = n!/(r!(n-r)!)). Books on a shelf: order matters (different arrangement = different outcome). Prize selection: order doesn't matter.
key_points: Permutation: order matters, P(n,r) = n!/(n-r)!
Combination: order doesn't matter, C(n,r) = n!/(r!(n-r)!)
5! = 120 — memorize factorials up to 10!
P(n,r) = C(n,r) × r!
tip: Quick check: 'how many ways to select' = combination. 'How many ways to arrange/seat/order' = permutation.
